query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Alloying the CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with a small amount of silver (Ag) will promote in situ formation of a lubricious Ag-rich surface film during sliding, thereby maintaining low friction coefficients and reduced wear rates over the full temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C relative to the undoped baseline alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy produced by conventional arc melting followed by homogenization annealing at around 1000 °C to achieve uniform, equiaxed grains.
generation.intervention: Introduce approximately 1–3 wt% Ag into the CoCrFeNi melt to achieve a uniform alloy where Ag is available to segregate to surfaces during use.
generation.conditions: Sliding wear tests conducted in ambient air under a fixed load (e.g., ~30 N) and representative sliding speeds. Tests are performed at discrete temperature steps (room temperature, intermediate temperatures such as 300 °C and 500 °C, and 800 °C) to cover the full operational range.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of Ag-rich nanoprecipitates or a continuous Ag-enriched film at the worn surface and along grain boundaries during sliding.
generation.mechanism: During sliding, the relatively low-melting, soft Ag phases diffuse and segregate to the contact surface. This produces a thin, continuous lubricious film that provides a low-shear-strength interface, reducing friction and wear. The film is expected to remain stable over a wide temperature range, with Ag’s stability near its melting temperature (961 °C) ensuring lubrication even at 800 °C.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline CoCrFeNi alloy, the Ag-doped alloy will exhibit a lower coefficient of friction and decreased wear rate across the full temperature range, with the lubricious Ag film mitigating degradation of tribological performance.
generation.baseline: The unalloyed CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy without Ag addition.
generation.boundary: The intervention is designed for tests in ambient air with sliding loads around 30 N, sliding speeds relevant for engineering applications, and test temperatures ranging from room temperature to 800 °C. The Ag addition is kept low (1–3 wt%) to avoid adverse effects on the overall mechanical integrity of the HEA.
generation.uncertainty: The exact optimal Ag wt% and the dynamics of Ag segregation during sliding are not fully established. There is also uncertainty regarding the long-term thermal stability of the Ag-rich film at temperatures approaching 800 °C and its possible interactions with oxidation processes in air.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of baseline CoCrFeNi alloy and one set of CoCrFeNi alloy doped with ~2 wt% Ag. Process both sets identically. Conduct sliding wear tests under the same conditions (ambient air, ~30 N load, fixed sliding speed) at room temperature, 300 °C, 500 °C, and 800 °C. Use surface analytical techniques (such as SEM, EDS, and XPS) to examine worn surfaces for Ag enrichment.
measurements: Measure the coefficient of friction at each temperature using a tribometer.
Quantify wear rate via mass loss and surface profilometry.
Analyze the chemical composition of worn surfaces for evidence of an Ag-rich lubricious film.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Ag-doped alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in friction coefficient and wear rate compared with the baseline at any tested temperature, or if no Ag-rich film is detected on the worn surfaces across the temperature range, then the hypothesis is falsified.
